transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-03-18
- Start: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Recording ID: ff-20250318-astacare-01
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (AstraCare Platform), Priya Nair (AstraCare Head ML), Sam Ortiz (AstraCare Security), Elena Morales (AstraCare SRE)

Summary / Agenda (auto-gen may be rough):
- Quick intro and goal setting (5m)
- Console walkthrough: traces, request logs, error analysis (30m)
- Q&A: RBAC, KMS, data retention, sampling (8m)
- Recap and next steps (5m)

Transcript:
[00:00:01] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya Chen on the Redwood side. I see Arjun's with me, he's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Jordan: Good, thanks. Jordan here, platform engineering at AstraCare. Priya and Sam are on as well.
[00:00:12] Priya: Hi all.
[00:00:14] Sam: Morning.
[00:00:16] Maya: Great. Goal for today is a focused console walkthrough — specifically tracing and request logs, error analysis and our debugging flows. We'll show request-level traces, how we correlate them with model invocations, and how you can replay or export requests for debugging.
[00:00:29] Arjun: I'll jump into the console, show a few live traces from the demo cluster and then walk through a simulated error where a client hit a fallback route. Note, this is the hosted demo environment so numbers aren't your production SLAs.
[00:00:40] Jordan: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in retention and whether we can set different policies per environment. Also Sam's concerned about PII and KMS.
[00:00:47] Maya: Yep, we'll cover that. Quick logistics: we'll share the recording and the security packet including SOC 2, encryption at rest and in transit, and our KMS integrations.

[00:01:10] -- Arjun shares screen --
[00:01:15] Arjun: Alright, this is the Redwood Console. Top nav: Models, Routes, Observability, Optimize. Going to Observability > Traces.
[00:01:26] Arjun: You can see a list of recent requests, each has a request ID, route, model variant, and latency. There's a column for fallback events, and an error badge where applicable. The UI lets you filter by route, model, and by time window.
[00:01:42] Priya: How granular are the traces? Do they show token-level latency or only end-to-end?
[00:01:49] Arjun: Good question. We capture per-stage spans: request ingestion, routing, model inference, kv cache hit/miss, and post-processing. Token-level timing is exposed for supported model runtimes — sometimes labeled as token-streaming, might show as 'stream' with approximate per-token timing. Note that for quantized/optimized kernels the token timings can be noisy.
[00:02:10] Sam: Are the traces sampled? What's retention?
[00:02:14] Arjun: By default traces are sampled at 1% for hosted, but you can set per-route sampling rules and increase for specific routes and time windows for debugging. Retention: traces metadata retained 90 days in hosted plan; raw request payloads are configurable — default 30 days, enterprise can set custom retention or disable retention. For Private we support custom policies on your side.
[00:02:33] Jordan: Can we redact PII before it's stored? We can't keep PHI in logs unencrypted.
[00:02:39] Arjun: We have two approaches: customer-side redaction via SDK hooks and server-side tokenization before storage. We also support KMS-managed encryption for stored payloads. In the console you can see redaction indicators — e g when a field is redacted it shows a redaction marker and the trace shows which redaction rule applied.
[00:02:58] Priya: If a trace shows a fallback, can we quickly find the signal that caused it? For example, model timeout vs rate limit vs safety filter.
[00:03:06] Arjun: Yes. Each trace includes an event timeline with annotated reasons: timeout, 429 rate-limit, safety-filter hit, and fallback invocation details. I'll open an example.
[00:03:18] [00:03:19] Arjun: Here's a trace where the primary model returned truncated output and the system routed to a smaller, low-cost variant as part of the fallback policy. You can expand the model span to see the model's response, the token count, and any warnings.
[00:03:33] Jordan: That model response text is redacted in the UI in your demo, I'm guessing for the recording?
[00:03:38] Arjun: Yeah, sometimes we mask long outputs in shared demos; in your tenant it's configurable.
[00:03:44] -- slight crosstalk --
[00:03:47] Sam: What's the audit trail for when someone replays or exports a request? We need an immutable log for compliance.
[00:03:53] Arjun: Every admin-level action is recorded in the audit logs. Replay/export actions show actor, timestamp, IP, and you can forward that to your SIEM via webhook or push to S3 with LFU. The audit record can't be edited via console.
[00:04:08] Priya: Can the console show correlation IDs from our upstream services so we can join logs?
[00:04:13] Arjun: Yep, you can pass an external_correlation_id header and it surfaces in the trace header and in request logs. We also integrate with vendor tracing like Datadog via trace forwarding.
[00:04:24] Jordan: Show us error analysis UI — I want to see grouping by error type.
[00:04:28] Arjun: Observability > Errors. Here's a grouped view. Errors are clustered by fingerprint (stack + code + route). You can click a cluster to see the top incidents, affected routes, and a sample trace. Clusters can be exported for trello or jira.
[00:04:43] Arjun: For example this cluster is a timeout spike — you can see spike graph, percent of requests affected and a couple of sample traces. There's also a blame timeline that points to model rollouts or infra events when available.
[00:04:55] Priya: How does this work with Dedicated and Private? Are traces collected locally?
[00:05:01] Maya: For Dedicated, we can ship observability metadata to your tenancy with two modes: metrics-only to our hosted console, or full telemetry forwarded to your VPC/S3. Private on-prem can keep all telemetry inside the tenant and integrate with your ELK/Datadog.
[00:05:14] Sam: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys for data at rest?
[00:05:18] Maya: Yes. KMS/HSM integrations supported, including AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM. We will share the integration guide in the security packet.
[00:05:27] Jordan: Walk me through a debugging flow end-to-end — an intermittent 500 for one of our routes.
[00:05:32] Arjun: Sure. Step 1: find error cluster in Errors tab. Step 2: open a representative trace and identify the model span and any infra spans. Step 3: check fallback history on the route to see if rolling back model variant correlates with error frequency. Step 4: if needed, replay the request in a sandbox with seeded traffic and captured environment headers. Replay is a one-click action, but it's auditable and you can toggle redaction.
[00:05:53] Priya: For replay, do you simulate exact timing and tokenization?
[00:05:57] Arjun: We replay the request into the model runtime with original request headers and can approximate the same tokenization. Timing will vary depending on current load, but we can throttle to replicate approximate QPS. For very precise perf testing we recommend a dedicated benchmark run.
[00:06:11] Jordan: Can we export a CSV of the trace timeline to correlate with our infra logs?
[00:06:15] Arjun: Yes, you can export a trace timeline as JSON or CSV, includes span start/end times and metadata.
[00:06:21] Sam: On RBAC — can we limit who can replay or who can see payloads?
[00:06:25] Maya: RBAC is role-based and you can create roles that restrict viewing payloads, allow redacted-only views, or disallow replay/export. We'll show the RBAC screen in a sec.
[00:06:33] -- Arjun navigates to Admin > Access control --
[00:06:36] Arjun: Here you can create a role 'SRE-readonly' and uncheck 'view_payloads' and 'request_replay'. Assign to a group via SAML.
[00:06:46] Elena: Do you support SCIM provisioning?
[00:06:49] Maya: Yes, SAML + SCIM supported. We'll include the IdP metadata template in the packet.
[00:06:56] Jordan: A little nit — sometimes our logs show lots of small failures that aren't actionable. Can we set alerting on error clusters?
[00:07:02] Arjun: Alerts can be configured on cluster thresholds or percent error rate per route. Alerts can push to PagerDuty, email, or webhook with incident context and a link to a playbook.
[00:07:12] Priya: Playbooks — can we attach a runbook to a cluster?
[00:07:15] Arjun: Yes, you can attach a markdown playbook to an error group and it shows up in the incident view.
[00:07:22] Jordan: How does sampling interact with alerting? If traces are sampled at 1% but alerts need full fidelity?
[00:07:28] Arjun: Traces are for debugging; metrics and error counts are separate and sampled at higher fidelity. Alerts use metrics (un-sampled counts) so sampling doesn't affect alert accuracy. You can bump trace sampling when investigating.
[00:07:39] Sam: Any third-party forwarding? We'd like to ship some telemetry to our Datadog account.
[00:07:44] Arjun: Yes, we have native Datadog, Sentry, and Splunk integrations for trace and metric forwarding. Also can push raw request logs to S3 or GCS.
[00:07:53] Jordan: Can you demonstrate a request with a safety filter hit and how it's shown in the trace?
[00:07:58] Arjun: Sure. Here's a trace with a safety-filter span, it shows the matched rule id, confidence score, and the action (block/score/warn). The trace shows the fallback and an annotation that the response was redacted.
[00:08:12] Priya: Do you keep the raw unredacted payload anywhere if redaction is on?
[00:08:17] Arjun: We can, but it's only stored if configured for ephemeral retention and with customer-managed KMS. Otherwise redacted data is not retained. For audits we can provide a time-limited unredacted export under an NDA.
[00:08:28] Jordan: Let's talk quotas and rate-limiting. If we hit a rate limit, does that surface in traces?
[00:08:33] Arjun: Yes, we annotate rate-limit events — 429s — and show spike graphs for the route. We also show per-token billing deltas so you can see cost impact.
[00:08:43] Elena: Any way to correlate model version rollouts with observed errors?
[00:08:47] Arjun: Rollouts are tied to model-version metadata in traces; you can filter traces by model-commit or rollout tag. The console shows a rollout timeline and can overlay error rate to visualize correlation.
[00:08:58] Priya: If we want to run this on Dedicated, are there additional observability agents?
[00:09:02] Arjun: For Dedicated we run a lightweight agent that ships spans to your VPC collector or our hosted endpoint depending on config. The agent also exposes Prometheus metrics for node-level telemetry.
[00:09:12] Jordan: Can the agent be air-gapped?
[00:09:15] Maya: For Private on-prem we support fully air-gapped installs; agent collects locally and writes to your chosen store.
[00:09:21] -- silence while Arjun pulls an example trace --
[00:09:34] Arjun: I'm opening a trace that shows a 500 from the post-processing function — looks like a JSON parse error in a custom post-processing lambda. You can see the stack, the input payload and the exact field that caused the parse to fail.
[00:09:46] Jordan: Nice. We have a lot of custom post-processing — being able to see the exact failure in-context helps.
[00:09:50] Priya: How do you handle user-supplied function calls in traces?
[00:09:53] Arjun: Function calls are recorded as spans with the payload (redacted per policy). You can drill into function logs and see return values. We can also forward those logs to your function log sink.
[00:10:03] Sam: Any built-in anomaly detection?
[00:10:06] Arjun: We have anomaly detection for latency and error rate using changepoint detection and windows. It surfaces anomalies in the Observability > Insights tab.
[00:10:15] Priya: Are tracing traces compatible with open standards like OpenTelemetry?
[00:10:19] Arjun: We accept OpenTelemetry spans via our collector and can export in OTLP. So you can join Redwood traces with your service traces.
[00:10:26] Maya: Quick note on cost: trace ingestion is metered — heavy trace sampling increases cost. For debugging we recommend bumping sampling temporarily. The Optimize product can analyze traces and suggest batching or KV cache rules to reduce per-token costs.
[00:10:40] Jordan: You mentioned request logs. How are logs structured and queried?
[00:10:44] Arjun: Request logs are JSON lines with request_id, route, model, timing spans, status, and metadata. You can query them in the Logs tab using simple filters or export to your SIEM. There's a console query bar that supports time-based filters and regex.
[00:10:58] Priya: Do logs include embeddings tokens or are those separate?
[00:11:01] Arjun: Embedding calls are logged separately but correlated by request_id.
[00:11:05] Jordan: If we want to wire custom dashboards, is there an API to pull logs and traces?
[00:11:09] Arjun: Yes, there's an Observability API for traces, logs, and metrics with pagination and filters. We'll give sample curl commands in the follow-up.
[00:11:18] Sam: Anything to call out on compliance for healthcare use?
[00:11:22] Maya: We'll include our HIPAA considerations — while Redwood provides the platform features needed (encryption, private deployment options, audit logs), customers must configure redaction and access rules. For PHI we recommend Private deployment or strict retention with KMS keys.
[00:11:34] Jordan: Last question: can we mask model responses in the UI for operators but still allow SREs to access unmasked copies for debugging?
[00:11:41] Arjun: Yes, role-based masking is supported — you can have 'operator' role see masked outputs, 'sre' role see unmasked under audit conditions. All accesses are logged.
[00:11:50] Maya: Ok quick recap — we'll send the SOC2 + KMS notes and the IdP/SCIM template. Arjun will run a Dedicated perf run using your sample prompts. Jordan will send sample traffic and an anonymized error log. We'll reconvene on 2025-03-27 to review rollout policies.
[00:12:06] Jordan: Thanks, that was super helpful.
[00:12:09] Priya: Appreciate it.
[00:12:10] Sam: Thanks.
[00:12:12] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with materials and the recording.

End of recording.
